sense: of time: in advance, looking to the future

terms.gloss: look ahead, plan ahead, provide for what is coming
evidence: Cic. Fam. 2.8.1: ab homine longē in posterum prōspiciente
Ter. Ph. 781–782: plāgae crēscunt, nisi prōspicis
terms.comment: “To think far ahead” is longē in posterum prōspicere; with ut or nē, to see to it beforehand that … (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: for the future, from now on
evidence: Caes. BC 1.3.1: laudat prōmptōs atque in posterum cōnfirmat
terms.comment: Also “till the next day”, short for in posterum diem (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: ahead of time, before the time; too soon
evidence: Traupman 270, 394: ahead of time, ante tempus
Cic. Tusc. 1.93: ante tempus morī miserum esse
terms.comment: Classically “before the proper time, too soon” (Lewis & Short); in good time is mātūrē (see early).

phrases.latin: praesēns quod fuerat malum in diem abiit: plāgae crēscunt, nisi prōspicis
phrases.english: the trouble that was here has only been put off: the beatings will pile up unless you think ahead

phrases.latin: sed ut ab homine longē in posterum prōspiciente futūra exspectō
phrases.english: but from a man who looks far ahead I expect news of what is to come

sources: Lewis & Short: prospicio · Lewis & Short: posterus · Lewis & Short: tempus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 270, 319, 394.
